objects.description: Fixed-size bitset representing a set of NUMA nodes using an array of unsigned long words. Size scales with NUMA_NUM_NODES macro (128 on x86/x86_64, otherwise 2048). Intended primarily for source compatibility; the modern API uses struct bitmask.

Heap-allocated, variable-size bitmask abstraction used throughout libnuma to represent sets of nodes or CPUs. The size field stores number of bits; maskp points to the underlying word array. Allocate and free via numa_bitmask_alloc()/numa_bitmask_free(). Many libnuma functions accept/return this type.

functions.name: numa_bitmask_isbitset
functions.signature: int numa_bitmask_isbitset(const struct bitmask *bm, unsigned int n);
functions.description: Tests whether bit n is set in the given bitmask.
requirements: bm must be a valid, initialized struct bitmask with maskp pointing to at least ceil(size/64) words.
n must be less than bm->size; behavior for n >= size is unknown (likely treated as clear).

functions.name: numa_bitmask_setall
functions.description: Sets all bits in the bitmask and returns bm.
requirements: bm must be a valid, initialized struct bitmask.

functions.name: numa_bitmask_clearall
functions.description: Clears all bits in the bitmask and returns bm.
requirements: bm must be a valid, initialized struct bitmask.

functions.name: numa_bitmask_setbit
functions.signature: struct bitmask *numa_bitmask_setbit(struct bitmask *bm, unsigned int n);
functions.description: Sets bit n in the bitmask and returns bm.
requirements: bm must be a valid, initialized struct bitmask.
n must be less than bm->size.

functions.name: numa_bitmask_clearbit
functions.signature: struct bitmask *numa_bitmask_clearbit(struct bitmask *bm, unsigned int n);
functions.description: Clears bit n in the bitmask and returns bm.
requirements: bm must be a valid, initialized struct bitmask.
n must be less than bm->size.

functions.name: numa_bitmask_nbytes
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes required to store the bitmask’s bits (based on bm->size).
requirements: bm must be a valid, initialized struct bitmask.

functions.name: numa_bitmask_weight
functions.description: Returns the number of bits set in the bitmask (population count).
requirements: bm must be a valid, initialized struct bitmask.

functions.name: numa_bitmask_alloc
functions.description: Allocates a new struct bitmask capable of holding nbits bits.
requirements: nbits must be greater than 0.
Caller must free the returned bitmask with numa_bitmask_free.

functions.name: numa_bitmask_free
functions.description: Frees a struct bitmask previously allocated by numa_bitmask_alloc or helpers that allocate bitmasks.
requirements: bm must either be NULL or a pointer returned by a compatible allocator (e.g., numa_bitmask_alloc, numa_allocate_nodemask, numa_allocate_cpumask).
Do not use bm after freeing.

functions.name: numa_bitmask_equal
functions.signature: int numa_bitmask_equal(const struct bitmask *a, const struct bitmask *b);
functions.description: Compares two bitmasks for equality. Returns nonzero if equal, zero otherwise.
requirements: a and b must be valid, initialized bitmask structures with comparable sizes; behavior for differing sizes is unknown.

functions.name: copy_nodemask_to_bitmask
functions.description: Copies bits from a legacy nodemask_t to a struct bitmask.
requirements: src must point to a valid nodemask_t.
dst must be a valid, initialized struct bitmask with maskp large enough to hold all bits of nodemask_t (typically via numa_allocate_nodemask).

functions.name: copy_bitmask_to_nodemask
functions.description: Copies bits from a struct bitmask into a legacy nodemask_t.
requirements: src must be a valid, initialized struct bitmask.
dst must point to a valid nodemask_t. Bits beyond nodemask_t capacity are truncated (exact behavior unspecified).

functions.name: copy_bitmask_to_bitmask
functions.description: Copies bits from one bitmask to another.
requirements: src and dst must be valid, initialized bitmasks.
dst must have capacity for src’s size; behavior on size mismatch is unknown.

functions.name: numa_available
functions.description: Checks whether NUMA support is available on this system. If this returns a negative value, all other functions in this library are undefined.
requirements: Must be called before using other libnuma functions; callers should verify return value is non-negative before proceeding.

functions.name: numa_max_node
functions.description: Returns the maximum available NUMA node index for the current environment.
requirements: Should be used only when numa_available() returned non-negative.
Return semantics beyond that are library-defined; negative values indicate error/unsupported.

functions.name: numa_max_possible_node
functions.description: Returns the maximum possible NUMA node index the kernel could expose.
requirements: Should be used only when numa_available() returned non-negative.

functions.name: numa_preferred
functions.description: Returns the current preferred NUMA node for allocations.
requirements: Should be used only when numa_available() returned non-negative.

functions.name: numa_preferred_err
functions.description: Returns the preferred node if available; returns an error if the preferred node is unavailable.
requirements: Should be used only when numa_available() returned non-negative.
Caller must check for error return (exact error codes unspecified).

functions.name: numa_node_size64
functions.signature: long long numa_node_size64(int node, long long *freep);
functions.description: Returns total memory size (bytes) of node and optionally stores free memory in *freep. Uses 64-bit values.
requirements: node should be a valid node id.
freep may be NULL to skip free memory output; if non-NULL, must point to writable long long.
Should be called only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_node_size
functions.description: Returns total memory size (bytes) of node and optionally stores free memory in *freep. 32-bit values.
requirements: node should be a valid node id.
freep may be NULL to skip free memory output; if non-NULL, must point to writable long.
Should be called only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_pagesize
functions.description: Returns the system page size used by libnuma’s allocation routines.
requirements: None beyond standard library initialization; typically after numa_available().

functions.name: numa_bind
functions.description: Restricts the calling process to run and allocate memory only on the specified set of nodes. Compatibility macro may redirect in version-1 builds.
requirements: nodes may be NULL (per version-1 macro behavior) but in this prototype it is a pointer; typical usage provides a valid bitmask.
Should be called only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_set_interleave_mask
functions.description: Sets the NUMA node interleaving mask for memory allocations. Pass 0/NULL to turn off interleaving.
requirements: If nodemask is non-NULL, it must be a valid bitmask of nodes.
Call only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_set_weighted_interleave_mask
functions.description: Sets a weighted interleaving mask for allocations. Pass 0/NULL to turn off weighted interleaving.
requirements: If nodemask is non-NULL it must be a valid weighted node bitmask per library’s format (details unspecified).
Call only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_get_interleave_mask
functions.description: Returns the current interleaving mask as a newly allocated bitmask.
requirements: Caller must free the returned bitmask with numa_bitmask_free.
Call only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_get_weighted_interleave_mask
functions.description: Returns the current weighted interleaving mask as a newly allocated bitmask.
requirements: Caller must free the returned bitmask with numa_bitmask_free.
Call only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_allocate_nodemask
functions.description: Allocates a bitmask big enough to represent all NUMA nodes.
requirements: Caller must free the returned bitmask with numa_bitmask_free.
Call only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_set_preferred
functions.description: Sets a single preferred NUMA node for the calling task’s memory allocations.
requirements: node should be a valid node id or a special value recognized by libnuma (details unspecified).
Call only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_has_preferred_many
functions.description: Reports whether the platform supports the MPOL_PREFERRED_MANY policy.
requirements: None specific; typically after numa_available().

functions.name: numa_set_preferred_many
functions.description: Sets a set of preferred nodes (preferred-many policy) for the calling task.
requirements: bitmask must be a valid bitmask; platform must support MPOL_PREFERRED_MANY (check with numa_has_preferred_many).
Call only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_preferred_many
functions.description: Returns the current set of preferred nodes for the calling task.
requirements: Caller must free the returned bitmask with numa_bitmask_free.
Call only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_set_localalloc
functions.description: Sets the memory allocation policy to prefer the local NUMA node.
requirements: Call only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_set_membind
functions.description: Restricts memory allocations to the specified set of nodes. Pass 0/NULL to turn off.
requirements: If nodemask is non-NULL it must be a valid bitmask of nodes.
Call only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_set_membind_balancing
functions.description: Restricts memory allocations to bmp nodes, optimizing page placement with kernel NUMA balancing if possible. Pass 0/NULL to turn off.
requirements: If bmp is non-NULL it must be a valid bitmask of nodes.
Call only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_get_membind
functions.description: Returns the current membind node set for the calling task as a newly allocated bitmask.
requirements: Caller must free the returned bitmask with numa_bitmask_free.
Call only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_get_mems_allowed
functions.description: Returns the set of memories (nodes) allowed to the calling task as a newly allocated bitmask.
requirements: Caller must free the returned bitmask with numa_bitmask_free.
Call only after successful numa_available().

functions.name: numa_get_interleave_node
functions.description: Returns the next interleave node or the node of a given address depending on policy (details unspecified).
requirements: Call only after successful numa_available().
Caller should check return value for errors; exact error codes unspecified.

functions.name: numa_alloc_interleaved_subset
functions.description: Allocates memory interleaved by page across the nodes in nodemask. Allocation is rounded to page size.
requirements: size must be > 0; will be rounded to page size.
nodemask must be a valid bitmask of nodes.
Memory must be freed with numa_free(ptr, size) using the same size value passed here.

functions.name: numa_alloc_interleaved
functions.description: Allocates memory interleaved by page across all nodes. Allocation is rounded to page size.
requirements: size must be > 0; will be rounded to page size.
Memory must be freed with numa_free(ptr, size) using the same size value passed here.

functions.name: numa_alloc_weighted_interleaved_subset
functions.description: Allocates memory interleaved across nodes according to weights encoded in nodemask. Rounded to page size.
requirements: size must be > 0; will be rounded to page size.
nodemask must be a valid weighted node bitmask per library format (details unspecified).
Memory must be freed with numa_free(ptr, size) using the same size value passed here.

functions.name: numa_alloc_weighted_interleaved
functions.description: Allocates memory interleaved across all nodes using current weighted interleave mask. Rounded to page size.
requirements: size must be > 0; will be rounded to page size.
Memory must be freed with numa_free(ptr, size) using the same size value passed here.

functions.name: numa_alloc_onnode
functions.description: Allocates memory on the specified NUMA node. Allocation is rounded to page size.
requirements: size must be > 0; will be rounded to page size.
node should be a valid node id.
Memory must be freed with numa_free(ptr, size) using the same size value passed here.

functions.name: numa_alloc_local
functions.description: Allocates memory on the local NUMA node. Allocation is rounded to page size.
requirements: size must be > 0; will be rounded to page size.
Memory must be freed with numa_free(ptr, size) using the same size value passed here.

functions.name: numa_alloc
functions.description: Allocates memory using the current memory policy. Allocation is rounded to page size.
requirements: size must be > 0; will be rounded to page size.
Memory must be freed with numa_free(ptr, size) using the same size value passed here.

functions.name: numa_realloc
functions.description: Changes the size of a memory area while preserving the NUMA memory policy.
requirements: old_addr must be a pointer returned by a libnuma allocator (or NULL for fresh allocation).
old_size and new_size are in bytes; sizes are rounded to page size.
If resizing, caller must later free with numa_free(new_ptr, new_size).

functions.name: numa_free
functions.description: Frees memory allocated by libnuma allocation functions. Size must match the size passed at allocation (rounded semantics per library).
requirements: mem must be a pointer returned by a libnuma allocation function.
size must be the same value supplied at allocation to ensure correct freeing.

functions.name: numa_interleave_memory
functions.signature: void numa_interleave_memory(void *mem, size_t size, struct bitmask *mask);
functions.description: Applies interleaving policy to an existing memory area. Intended for memory not yet touched.
requirements: mem must point to the start of the memory area; size in bytes (rounded to page size).
mask must be a valid bitmask of nodes.
The memory must not have been touched before applying the policy.

functions.name: numa_weighted_interleave_memory
functions.signature: void numa_weighted_interleave_memory(void *mem, size_t size, struct bitmask *mask);
functions.description: Applies weighted interleaving policy to an existing memory area. Intended for memory not yet touched.
requirements: mem must point to the start of the memory area; size in bytes (rounded to page size).
mask must be a valid weighted bitmask of nodes.
The memory must not have been touched before applying the policy.

functions.name: numa_tonode_memory
functions.signature: void numa_tonode_memory(void *start, size_t size, int node);
functions.description: Applies a policy to allocate (back) a memory area on a specific node. Intended for low-level/shared memory setup before touching pages.
requirements: start must point to the memory region; size in bytes (rounded to page size).
node should be a valid node id.
The memory must not be touched before policy is applied.

functions.name: numa_tonodemask_memory
functions.signature: void numa_tonodemask_memory(void *mem, size_t size, struct bitmask *mask);
functions.description: Applies a policy to allocate (back) a memory area on the nodes in mask. Intended for low-level/shared memory before touching pages.
requirements: mem must point to the memory region; size in bytes (rounded to page size).
mask must be a valid bitmask of nodes.
The memory must not be touched before policy is applied.

functions.name: numa_setlocal_memory
functions.description: Applies local-node allocation policy to a memory area. Intended for memory not yet touched.
requirements: start must point to the memory region; size in bytes (rounded to page size).
The memory must not be touched before policy is applied.

functions.name: numa_police_memory
functions.description: Applies the current memory policy to a region (enforce policy on allocation). Intended for memory not yet touched.
requirements: start must point to the memory region; size in bytes (rounded to page size).
The memory must not be touched before policy is applied.

functions.name: numa_run_on_node_mask
functions.description: Constrains the current task to run only on CPUs in the given node mask (cpus of those nodes).
requirements: mask must be a valid bitmask of nodes.
Caller should check return value for errors (nonzero indicates failure per typical convention; exact semantics unspecified).

functions.name: numa_run_on_node_mask_all
functions.description: Constrains the current task to run only on CPUs in mask, ignoring cpusets awareness.
requirements: mask must be a valid bitmask of nodes.
Caller should check return value for errors.

functions.name: numa_run_on_node
functions.description: Constrains the current task to run only on the specified node.
requirements: node should be a valid node id.
Caller should check return value for errors.

functions.name: numa_get_run_node_mask
functions.description: Returns the current mask of nodes the task can run on as a newly allocated bitmask.
requirements: Caller must free the returned bitmask with numa_bitmask_free.

functions.name: numa_set_bind_policy
functions.description: Controls bind policy behavior: when strict is set, fail allocation if memory cannot be allocated on target node(s).
requirements: strict is treated as boolean (nonzero enables strict).
Affects subsequent allocation calls; ensure numa_available() succeeded.

functions.name: numa_set_strict
functions.description: Controls strictness: fail when existing memory has incompatible policy.
requirements: flag is treated as boolean (nonzero enables strict behavior).

functions.name: numa_num_possible_nodes
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of nodes (size of kernel nodemask_t).
requirements: None; typically after numa_available().

functions.name: numa_num_possible_cpus
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of CPUs (size of kernel cpumask_t).
requirements: None.

functions.name: numa_num_configured_nodes
functions.description: Returns the number of nodes configured in the system.
requirements: None.

functions.name: numa_num_configured_cpus
functions.description: Returns the number of CPUs configured in the system.
requirements: None.

functions.name: numa_num_task_cpus
functions.description: Returns the maximum CPUs allowed to the current task.
requirements: None.

functions.name: numa_num_thread_cpus
functions.description: Backward compatibility alias: returns the maximum CPUs allowed to the current thread/task.
requirements: None.

functions.name: numa_num_task_nodes
functions.description: Returns the maximum nodes allowed to the current task.
requirements: None.

functions.name: numa_num_thread_nodes
functions.description: Backward compatibility alias: returns the maximum nodes allowed to the current thread/task.
requirements: None.

functions.name: numa_allocate_cpumask
functions.description: Allocates a bitmask sized to the kernel’s cpumask_t.
requirements: Caller must free the returned bitmask with numa_bitmask_free.

functions.name: numa_node_to_cpus
functions.description: Fills cpumask with CPUs that belong to the given node. Returns 0 on success, -1 and sets errno on failure.
requirements: node should be a valid node id.
cpumask must be a valid, allocated bitmask sized for CPUs (e.g., via numa_allocate_cpumask).
Caller must check return value and errno on failure.

functions.name: numa_node_to_cpu_update
functions.description: Updates internal mappings used by numa_node_to_cpus (e.g., after topology changes).
requirements: None; call before numa_node_to_cpus if topology may have changed.

functions.name: numa_node_of_cpu
functions.description: Returns the NUMA node of the specified CPU, or -1 and sets errno on invalid CPU.
requirements: cpu should be a valid CPU id.
Caller must check for -1 and use errno on error.

functions.name: numa_distance
functions.description: Returns distance of node1 from node2; returns 0 on error.
requirements: node1 and node2 should be valid node ids.
Caller must treat 0 as an error indicator.

functions.name: numa_error
functions.description: Internal libnuma error handler that can be overridden by user programs. Default behavior prints an error to stderr and may exit if numa_exit_on_error is true.
requirements: where must be a non-NULL descriptive string of the call site.
If overridden, replacement must match this signature.

functions.name: numa_warn
functions.description: Warning function (overridable). Default prints a formatted message to stderr once; may exit if numa_exit_on_warn is true.
requirements: fmt must be a non-NULL printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match format.
If overridden, replacement must match this signature.

functions.name: numa_migrate_pages
functions.signature: int numa_migrate_pages(int pid, struct bitmask *from, struct bitmask *to);
functions.description: Requests migration of a task’s pages from nodes in ‘from’ to nodes in ‘to’.
requirements: pid identifies the target process.
from and to must be valid node bitmasks.
Caller must check return value for success/failure; exact errno codes unspecified.

functions.name: numa_move_pages
functions.signature: int numa_move_pages(int pid, unsigned long count, void **pages, const int *nodes, int *status, int flags);
functions.description: Moves or queries locations of individual pages for a process. Wrapper around move_pages syscall semantics.
requirements: pid identifies the target process.
count specifies number of pages; arrays pages, nodes (if moving), and status must have at least count elements.
pages must contain page-aligned addresses for the target process.
nodes may be NULL to query; otherwise must contain target node ids for each page.
status must be non-NULL and writable; receives per-page results.
flags control behavior (see move_pages).

functions.name: numa_sched_getaffinity
functions.description: Gets the CPU affinity of a process into a bitmask.
requirements: pid is the target process id (0 for calling process, per usual semantics).
mask must be a valid, allocated cpumask-sized bitmask.
Caller must check return value for errors.

functions.name: numa_sched_setaffinity
functions.description: Sets the CPU affinity of a process from a bitmask.
requirements: pid is the target process id (0 for calling process, per usual semantics).
mask must be a valid, allocated cpumask-sized bitmask populated with desired CPUs.
Caller must check return value for errors.

functions.name: numa_parse_nodestring
functions.description: Parses an ASCII list/range string of node ids into a bitmask, respecting current nodeset constraints.
requirements: s must be a NUL-terminated string in the accepted list/range syntax (details unspecified).
Caller must free the returned bitmask with numa_bitmask_free.

functions.name: numa_parse_nodestring_all
functions.description: Parses an ASCII list/range of node ids into a bitmask without current nodeset dependency.
requirements: s must be a NUL-terminated string in accepted syntax.
Caller must free the returned bitmask with numa_bitmask_free.

functions.name: numa_parse_cpustring
functions.description: Parses an ASCII list/range of CPU ids into a bitmask, respecting current taskset constraints.
requirements: s must be a NUL-terminated string in accepted syntax.
Caller must free the returned bitmask with numa_bitmask_free.

functions.name: numa_parse_cpustring_all
functions.description: Parses an ASCII list/range of CPU ids into a bitmask without current taskset dependency.
requirements: s must be a NUL-terminated string in accepted syntax.
Caller must free the returned bitmask with numa_bitmask_free.

functions.name: numa_has_home_node
functions.description: Returns whether the system supports setting a home_node for mbind and preferred_many.
requirements: None.

functions.name: numa_set_mempolicy_home_node
functions.signature: int numa_set_mempolicy_home_node(void *start, unsigned long len, int home_node, int flags);
functions.description: Sets the home node for a VMA policy present in the task’s address range [start, start+len).
requirements: start is the start address; len is the length in bytes.
home_node should be a valid node id.
flags controls behavior (values unspecified here).
Caller must check return value for errors.

functions.name: get_mempolicy
functions.signature: long get_mempolicy(int *mode, unsigned long *nmask, unsigned long maxnode, void *addr, unsigned flags);
functions.description: Kernel syscall interface to query memory policy. Returns policy mode and node mask per flags.
requirements: mode may be NULL or a pointer to receive policy mode.
nmask may be NULL or a buffer to receive bitmask up to maxnode bits.
maxnode specifies the maximum number of nodes represented (bit count).
addr is used when MPOL_F_ADDR is set; otherwise ignored.
flags controls query behavior (MPOL_F_NODE, MPOL_F_ADDR, MPOL_F_MEMS_ALLOWED).
Caller must check return value (negative indicates error, sets errno).

functions.name: mbind
functions.signature: long mbind(void *start, unsigned long len, int mode, const unsigned long *nmask, unsigned long maxnode, unsigned flags);
functions.description: Kernel syscall interface to set memory policy for a given address range.
requirements: start is the start address; len is the length in bytes.
mode must be one of MPOL_* values.
nmask may be NULL or a pointer to a bitmask; required for some modes.
maxnode is the number of bits in nmask (maximum node id + 1).
flags may include MPOL_MF_STRICT, MPOL_MF_MOVE, MPOL_MF_MOVE_ALL.
Caller must check return value (negative indicates error, sets errno).

functions.name: set_mempolicy
functions.signature: long set_mempolicy(int mode, const unsigned long *nmask, unsigned long maxnode);
functions.description: Kernel syscall interface to set the calling thread’s default memory policy.
requirements: mode must be one of MPOL_* values.
nmask may be NULL or a pointer to a bitmask; required for some modes.
maxnode is the number of bits in nmask (maximum node id + 1).
Caller must check return value (negative indicates error, sets errno).

functions.name: migrate_pages
functions.signature: long migrate_pages(int pid, unsigned long maxnode, const unsigned long *frommask, const unsigned long *tomask);
functions.description: Kernel syscall interface to migrate a task’s pages from one set of nodes to another.
requirements: pid identifies the target process.
maxnode is the number of bits in frommask/tomask.
frommask and tomask must be bitmasks (may be NULL in some kernels for queries; specifics outside this header).
Caller must check return value (negative indicates error, sets errno).

functions.name: move_pages
functions.signature: long move_pages(int pid, unsigned long count, void **pages, const int *nodes, int *status, int flags);
functions.description: Kernel syscall interface to move or query individual pages for a process.
requirements: pid identifies the target process.
count is number of pointers in arrays; must be > 0 for nontrivial calls.
pages must be a pointer to an array of page addresses in the target process.
nodes may be NULL (query) or point to an array of target node ids.
status must be non-NULL to receive per-page results.
flags controls behavior (kernel-defined).
Caller must check return value (negative indicates error, sets errno).

functions.name: set_mempolicy_home_node
functions.signature: int set_mempolicy_home_node(void *start, unsigned long len, int home_node, int flag);
functions.description: Kernel interface to set the home node for a VMA policy in the address range [start, start+len).
requirements: start is the start address; len is the length in bytes.
home_node should be a valid node id.
flag controls behavior (values unspecified here).
Caller must check return value for errors (negative indicates error with errno).

data_types.description: An ASCII, NUL-terminated string encoding a set of NUMA node IDs using list/range syntax. Typical accepted forms include comma-separated IDs and inclusive ranges, e.g., "0", "1,3,5", "0-3", "0-2,4,6-8". Whitespace may or may not be allowed depending on parser; IDs are non-negative integers; ranges use a single hyphen with start<=end.

An ASCII, NUL-terminated string encoding a set of CPU IDs using list/range syntax. Typical accepted forms include comma-separated IDs and inclusive ranges, e.g., "0", "1,3,5", "0-3", "0-2,4,6-8". Whitespace may or may not be allowed depending on parser; IDs are non-negative integers; ranges use a single hyphen with start<=end.
